name: Seafood and fish markets
shape_facts: Retail shop, wholesale stall at a market, auction trader, exporter, or restaurant supplier
Buying from auction, own/partner boats, farmers (aquaculture), or importers
Fresh vs frozen share, and processing (cleaning, filleting, packing)
Cold storage and ice supply arrangements
Customer mix: households, restaurants/hotels, export buyers, online
Number of stalls/shops and staff (cleaners, cutters, drivers)
Export documentation handled in-house or by an agent
scope_rule: pi notes operational problems: daily price swings, spoilage, ice and cold-chain downtime, weighing and cleaning loss, credit to restaurants, export shipment coordination and reporting. It does not advise on fishing seasons and bans, export certification, sanitary/phytosanitary rules, customs, food safety or tax. It does not record names of boat owners, buyers, staff or customers, and never takes bank or payment details.

vocabulary.cleaning charge: fee for gutting, scaling and cutting
vocabulary.glaze: ice coating on frozen seafood, adds weight

problems.phrase: Fish not sold by afternoon loses value, by night it’s gone
Auction prices change every morning and I can’t keep up my retail price
After cleaning, weight drops and I don’t know my real cost
Ice supply runs out on hot days
Freezer and cold store breakdowns
Diesel for the generator is a huge cost
Cleaners keep the best pieces or take cash for cleaning
Scale disputes with customers
Restaurants and hotels pay 60–90 days late
Export shipment delayed and the buyer cancelled
Export documents take days and we miss the vessel
Glazing and weight complaints from buyers abroad
Which variety makes money? I have no idea
Ledger with boat owners for advances is all in a register
Prices in dirhams/dollars swing and I lose on export margin
WhatsApp orders from restaurants overnight, someone misses one
Rider delivers fish late and the restaurant rejects it
Supply drops in certain months and customers move to another supplier
Cutters are hard to keep in summer
Stock in cold store doesn’t match the book
No way to show daily catch to customers online
Cleaning area hygiene complaints
Two stalls, I don’t know which is profitable

spoilage: How much is usually unsold at the end of the day?
buying: Where do you buy — auction, boats, farms or importers?
pricing: How often do you change your selling price?
cleaning: Do you track weight before and after cleaning?
cold chain: How do you store unsold stock?
How often does ice or the freezer let you down?
credit: How many restaurants or hotels buy on credit?
orders: How do trade orders reach you?
stock: Does the cold store count match your book?
reporting: Can you see which fish makes money?

seasons: - PK: winter is peak fish season and demand ( machhli with rain and cold); fishing restrictions/closures in parts of the year affect supply (pi notes the effect only, not the rules); Lent and Christmas for Christian customers; Ramadan iftar fried fish; summer heat raises spoilage. - UAE: cooler months raise demand; seasonal fishing restrictions on certain species affect supply (pi notes the effect only); Ramadan and Eid; tourism season for hotels and restaurants. - Canada: lobster, crab and salmon seasons by region; Lent and Easter; Christmas Eve seafood; summer cottage and BBQ season.
care: Cold-room entrapment, knife injuries, slips, boat accidents or ammonia leaks: pi points to emergency services immediately.
Fishing bans, species restrictions, export certification and customs: no advice; pi notes the admin effort only.
Requests to mislabel species, origin, or over-glaze to inflate weight: pi declines.
Requests to under-invoice exports or move cash informally: pi declines.
Boat owners, buyers and staff are recorded by role only.
build_ideas: Daily buying log by species: source, weight, price, with yield after cleaning
Cost per kg after cleaning and selling-price helper using the owner’s margin rule
Unsold stock and markdown log by species and day
Cold-store stock book with in/out and count variance
Ice and freezer downtime log with costs
Trade order intake via WhatsApp form, with a consolidated morning dispatch list
Restaurant/hotel credit ledger with statements and reminders
Boat advance ledger by boat label, with settlements per landing
Export shipment tracker: buyer order, packing, document checklist status, vessel cut-off dates, with currency noted per order
Daily catch broadcast to opted-in customers with today’s prices

exchange.text: Every morning I buy at the auction and by evening a lot is still sitting there. Restaurants also pay so late.
Noted — unsold fish by evening, and slow payments from restaurants. Which of those is hurting you more right now?
The payments. Some owe for three months.
Got it, noted as the bigger one. Roughly how many restaurant or hotel accounts buy from you on credit?
Thanks, noted. How do you keep track of what each one owes today?
